title: Verify the observation channel before concluding absence
procedure: Before reporting that something is missing, empty or unreadable, check how the observation was made. Identify filters, truncation, symlink handling, access rights and flag semantics of the tool used. Re-observe through a second, independent method. Only then state absence; otherwise label it unverified.
components: List ways the tool could hide the target
Report absence only if both agree, else mark unverified
preconditions: A negative or surprising observation exists
An alternative observation method is available
limits: Costs an extra check on every negative result
Alternative method may share the same blind spot
counterexamples: Trivially reliable lookups where the tool is known exact and a second check adds only cost
Cases where an independent method is unavailable, so verification stalls progress

title: Reconcile contradictions before asserting
procedure: When two observations conflict, do not pick the one fitting your first story. Treat the conflict as a signal that one view is partial. Test each source for truncation, filtering, staleness or wrong scope, find the discriminating observation, and only then assert; retract promptly if a claim was already made.
components: State both observations side by side
Test each for truncation, filtering or staleness
Run a discriminating check, then assert or retract

triggers: process runs but file not listed

preconditions: Both observations are reproducible or inspectable
limits: Some contradictions stem from real state changes between observations, not partial views
counterexamples: Fast-changing systems where the contradiction is a genuine race and not an artifact of tooling

title: Trace context across each boundary
procedure: When behavior differs between components, hosts or chained processes, do not assume inheritance or direct paths. Enumerate each boundary (spawn, proxy, host, config scope), inspect what environment, identity or settings actually arrive on the far side, and locate the first boundary where expected context is lost, before editing code.
components: Inspect actual context received at each
Fix at the first boundary where it diverges

triggers: works in parent but not child
dependency not found in spawned process

preconditions: Ability to inspect state inside or at each hop
limits: Chains with many hops make full tracing expensive
Inspection may itself perturb the environment
counterexamples: Failures that are genuine code bugs in the first component, where boundary tracing wastes effort

title: Prefer one deferred read over repeated polling
procedure: For slow or costly remote operations, redirect output to a durable file or log, let the job run, and read the result once at an expected completion point. Poll only when intermediate state changes a decision, and then at widening intervals.
components: Redirect output to a durable artifact
Read once; poll only if state affects a decision
limits: Unsuitable when early failure detection saves more than polling costs
counterexamples: Jobs likely to fail early or hang, where early detection avoids larger waste
